company_name: Meridian Robotics, Inc. (fictional — not a real company)
note: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE, not a real SEC filing or real company. Constructed to test the SKILL.md instruction (Workflow step 3) that a Rule depending on an already-computed Attribute must reuse that Attribute's answer rather than re-deriving the same underlying fact independently. Article THIRD gives the Corporation an unusually specific, clearly breachable purpose clause (a named activity, named beneficiary classes, and a measurable 2%-of-net-income commitment) — enough to make Mission Existence and Breachability 'Affirmative' on its own terms — but the document contains no public benefit corporation election and no reference to Subchapter XV or Section 362 anywhere. A model that reuses the Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) Status attribute (confidently 'No') should reach 'Not affirmative' for Paramount Purpose quickly and without hedging, since that rule's Affirmative Condition requires PBC-or-equivalent status. A model that instead re-derives Paramount Purpose independently from how specific or values-driven the purpose clause reads risks answering 'Affirmative' or hedging to 'Could not determine' — mistaking a specific-but-ordinary purpose clause for a legally paramount one.

documents.note: Ordinary Delaware corporation — no PBC/Subchapter XV designation anywhere — with an unusually specific, named-beneficiary, measurable purpose clause and an ordinary (simple-majority) amendment provision.

designed_to_test: Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) Status: No (confident negative — no statutory designation anywhere in the document)
Stated Purpose: specific, quotable language (not boilerplate, not 'Could not determine')
Mission Existence and Breachability: Affirmative (names beneficiaries, a specific activity, and a measurable commitment)
Paramount Purpose: Not affirmative — MUST be grounded in the PBC Status attribute's 'No' rather than re-assessed independently from the purpose clause's specificity
Mission Protection from Ordinary Majority: Not affirmative (ordinary majority amendment provision, no lock-holding body, no federated/member constitution)
